text:
maria: FYI saw a small but consistent tail latency spike on canary after the latest loader change. stacktrace points to a bunch of short stalls during shard eviction + warmup handoff. attaching log excerpt below

maria: ```
[2026-03-19T21:14:33Z] warmup: request 0x7f -> start loading shard model-a/part-3
[2026-03-19T21:14:33Z] eviction: choosing victim part-12 (last_used=3s, refcnt=0)
[2026-03-19T21:14:33Z] handoff: pausing requests -> migrating kv for part-3 -> 45ms
[2026-03-19T21:14:33Z] request 0x7f -> resumed -> served after 120ms
```

jake: thanks, that matches the traces I saw. quick question: are those nodes under memory pressure or is this an ordering problem between eviction and warmup?

maria: mem pressure is moderate. more of a race: warmup kicks off async load for a shard, eviction decides victim in parallel, we currently revoke pages from the victim which triggers page faults and stalls the same IO pool warmup uses.

sylvie: ugh. this is the classic handoff vs evict ordering. two quick levers: 1) prefer non-overlapping IO queues (hardish), 2) change tiebreaker so warmup wins if it has an active request.

jake: option 2 seems lower-risk. what about the safetensors/manifest interaction? if we do index-first reads we can get metadata cheaply and avoid full scans during warmup. but index reads still hit the same disk device when sharded.

sylvie: right — index-first helps rank shards for warmup but doesn't eliminate eviction stalls. we should make warmup acquire a soft lease on the shard: soft lease prevents eviction until lease expires or explicit revoke. cheap lease = atomic flag in shared mem + grace window.

kevin: note: leases allocate a tiny byte of state per shard, but we need a tiebreaker when two models both want the last free page. ideas:
- prefer active request holders (requests in-flight within last 100ms)
- then prefer higher hotness (recentPrefixHits)
- then LRU

kevin: naive pseudo:
```
score(shard) = 1000*has_inflight + 10*recent_prefix_hits - age_seconds
victim = min(score)
```

maria: that looks reasonable. can we keep the constants configurable per deployment class (hosted vs dedicated)? hosted might prefer lower latency (so bias to warmup), dedicated might prefer deterministic throughput (so bias to LRU).

jake: agreed. also short-term mitigation: increase handoff grace window from 50ms -> 200ms on the canary fleet and disable immediate compaction during warmup. should reduce the observed 120ms stalls.

sylvie: small caution: longer grace means memory could be slightly less available under extremes. but 200ms is fine for canary tests. we should add telemetry for lease_wait_time and eviction_retries to see effect.

maria: action items:
- jake: roll canary with grace=200ms + compaction=off (today)
- sylvie: prepare RFC for Lease-based handoff + tiebreaker scoring (this week)
- kevin: add metrics: lease_acquire_time, lease_conflicts, victim_score_dist (next sprint)

deploy-bot: canary-deploy v2026.3.19-loaderfix started (id: dpl-5890) :rocket:

jake: on it, rolling now. will post perf numbers in #eng-ml once stable. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks everyone. if the canary still shows tail, we'll try index-first prefetch for safetensors on the next patch.

kevin: one more note for the RFC: include perf microbench for safetensors index vs header-only reads across spinning disk and nvme. that data will guide defaults.

sylvie: noted. i'll include a toy harness and results matrix.

maria: closing the thread for now. feel free to @maria if you need infra creds for testing. :white_check_mark:
